content.text:
This confirms it: before e44a62e, `retargetTrack` unconditionally called `sourceTrack.getTimes()` without a null check, causing an NPE whenever a mapped bone had no source track. Commit e44a62e "fixed" that NPE by adding `if (sourceTrack != null)` around the whole track-add logic — but this caused a different bug: bones without a source track were now silently skipped instead of getting a track (e.g. a bind-pose track), so the resulting animation would be missing tracks for those bones ("retargeting logic error"). Commit cd415ee fixes this correctly by generating a single-keyframe bind-pose track when `sourceTrack == null`, rather than skipping the bone entirely.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: e44a62e455053aed84a67fb57d5ab82e27491202

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `src/main/java/maud/Util.java`'s `retargetAnimation`/`retargetTrack` methods using `git log --follow`. The commit `cd415ee` (bug fix) removes an `if (sourceTrack != null)` guard that caused bones without a source track to be entirely skipped when building the retargeted animation, and instead makes `retargetTrack` synthesize a bind-pose track (single keyframe at t=0) when `sourceTrack == null`.

**(2) Specific change:** Looking at `e44a62e` ("bugfix: NPE in Util.retargetAnimation()"), I found the exact origin of this guard. Prior to that commit, `retargetTrack` unconditionally did `sourceTrack.getTimes()` on a track obtained via `MyAnimation.findTrack(...)`, which threw an NPE if the mapped source bone had no track in the animation. `e44a62e` fixed the NPE by adding `if (sourceTrack != null) { ...; result.addTrack(track); }` in `retargetAnimation`, i.e., it simply skipped adding a track for that bone rather than handling the null case properly. This introduced the "retargeting logic error": target bones without a corresponding source track ended up with no track at all in the result animation (instead of a bind-pose track), which is precisely the defect that `cd415ee` fixes.

**(3) Evidence:** The diff of `e44a62e` shows the introduction of the skip-on-null logic (`if (sourceTrack != null) { ... result.addTrack(track); }`), and the diff of `cd415ee` shows the exact removal of that same guard, replaced with unconditional `result.addTrack(track)` plus null-handling inside `retargetTrack` to build a bind-pose track. The intervening commit `772fb53` ("replace Util methods with ones from the heart library") touches the same file but does not alter this null-check logic (confirmed it carries the same `if (sourceTrack != null)` structure forward unchanged based on the diff context in `cd415ee` matching pre-772fb53 code paths). Thus the bug was introduced in `e44a62e` and persisted until fixed in `cd415ee`.

I'm confident in this identification since the fix commit's diff is essentially the exact inverse of the change made in `e44a62e`.
